statement: The function returns a result res. Let a plateau be a pair (a,b) such that 0 <= a <= b < len(nums), nums[a] = nums[a+1] = ... = nums[b], (a = 0 or nums[a-1] != nums[a]), and (b = len(nums)-1 or nums[b+1] != nums[b]). A plateau (a,b) is a hill if a > 0, b < len(nums)-1, nums[a-1] < nums[a], and nums[b+1] < nums[a]. It is a valley if a > 0, b < len(nums)-1, nums[a-1] > nums[a], and nums[b+1] > nums[a]. Then res is equal to the number of plateaus that are either a hill or a valley.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 3 and 100 inclusive, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.
